subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 08, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 08, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

As we continue to move forward with our mission to create a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution, we wanted to take a moment to highlight some recent developments and updates from the community.

Firstly, the Asahi Linux developers have released a new progress report for their Linux distribution for Apple devices. This is an exciting development, as it has the potential to bring Linux to a new and wider audience. We're keeping an eye on their progress and look forward to seeing the results.

In other community news, Amutable Foundations: A Technical Overview has been published, providing a detailed look at the technical aspects of this innovative project. We're always eager to learn more about the latest advancements in the world of Linux and open-source software.

The X.Org Developers Conference (XDC) took place recently, and videos from the event are now available online. If you're interested in learning more about the latest developments in the world of X.Org, we recommend checking out the videos.

On the AcreetionOS front, we've been working hard to improve our distribution and make it even more user-friendly. Our latest commit, intelligence sync: newsletter + archive + wiki guides + feed 2026-11-07-0338, has brought some exciting new features to the table. We're always looking for ways to improve our distribution and make it more accessible to our users.

We've also been working on fixing some issues that have been reported by our community. The fix postinstall.sh silently failing on pwfeedback sudoers edit in AcreetionOS-Xlibre is now resolved, and we're grateful for the community's help in identifying and reporting these issues.

In other news, we've been making some changes to our infrastructure. The ci: pass -R to gh release create (no checkout in release job) commit in acreetionos-immutable is part of our ongoing efforts to improve our build and release process.

We'd like to take a moment to thank our community for their continued support and engagement. Your feedback and contributions are invaluable to us, and we're grateful for the opportunity to work together to create a better Linux distribution.

As always, we're committed to transparency and open communication. If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
